newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-DRUMMOND WITHIN SHOE WIDTH OF PREMATURE EXIT.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-DRUMMOND WITHIN SHOE WIDTH OF PREMATURE EXIT.

text.p: American 200 metres champion Jon Drummond came within a shoe width of a premature exit from the world championships on Wednesday when he lost his balance in the final metres of his first round heat.
In what appeared at first to be premature victory celebrations, Drummond shot his right arm high in the air while well clear of the field.
At the same time he slowed and was lucky to finish in third place and win a place in the second round.
Drummond explained he had tilted off-balance and thrown out his right arm to avoid stepping out of lane and incurring automatic disqualification.
"I twisted my torso and held up my arm to keep balance," Drummond said. "I looked up at the scoreboard and was worried that I would see a DNF (did not finish) or DQ (disqualifed).
"When it said Q (qualified), I said 'Lord, thanks. I owe you one'."
Namibia's 1993 world champion Frankie Fredericks, who has been hampered by a injury to his right knee, complained about the hard track after finishing second in his heat.
"This injury has been with me all season and this hard track has made it worse," he said.
France's double champion Marie-Jose Perec made hard work of her first round heat in the women's 200 metres and confessed she would need something special to win a medal here.
Breathing heavily after winning her heat in 22.87 seconds, Perec said: "It would need a miracle for me to win a medal."

Cuba's Ana Fidelia Quirot opened her defence of the women's 800 metres title with a comfortable victory in her first round heat. Maria Mutola, the 1993 champion, was similarly untroubled in winning her heat.

Britain's defending champion Jonathan Edwards qualified easily for the triple jump final on Friday with his first jump of 17.28 metres. Olympic champion Kenny Harrison also needed just one leap of 17.11 to qualify.
There was less happy news for the Czech Republic's former Olympic champion Robert Zmelik who ran into a barrier and did not finish in the decathlon high hurdles, first event of the second day.
